learn: Fast facts come from strategies you can use in your head.
Doubles (7 + 7 = 14) and near doubles (7 + 8 = 15) are quick.
Making ten is another: 9 + 6 is 10 + 5 = 15.
lessons.try: Solve 8 + 7 two different ways.

learn: Think addition to subtract: 15 - 9 means 9 + ? = 15. The answer is 6.
Count up from the smaller number: from 9 to 15 is 6.
Subtracting from 10 is easy if you know your tens facts: 10 - 3 = 7.
lessons.try: Solve 16 - 8 by thinking addition.

learn: A fact family shows how three numbers work together: 6 + 7 = 13, 7 + 6 = 13, 13 - 6 = 7, 13 - 7 = 6.
Practise facts a little every day to make them automatic.
When facts are fast, harder problems are easier.
check: Which is in the fact family 6, 7, 13?
lessons.try: Write the fact family for 5, 9 and 14.

learn: An even number of objects can be put into pairs with none left over.
An odd number always has one left over.
6 socks make 3 pairs: even. 7 socks make 3 pairs and 1 extra: odd.
lessons.try: Pair up a pile of buttons. Is the number odd or even?

learn: You can tell if a number is even by looking at its ones digit.
If it ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, it is even.
If it ends in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9, it is odd.
check: Which digit makes a number odd?
lessons.try: Decide if 34, 57, 80 and 91 are odd or even.

learn: An even number can be written as a doubles fact: 12 = 6 + 6.
An odd number cannot be split into two equal whole numbers: 11 = 5 + 6.
This is another way to check odd and even.
check: Can 11 be split into two equal whole numbers?
lessons.try: Write 10, 14 and 18 as doubles.

learn: Ten tens make one hundred.
A three-digit number has hundreds, tens and ones. In 352, there are 3 hundreds, 5 tens and 2 ones.
352 = 300 + 50 + 2. This is expanded form.
lessons.try: Show 246 with drawings of hundreds squares, tens sticks and ones dots.

learn: 407 is read "four hundred seven". The zero holds the tens place.
Numbers can be written as digits, words or expanded form.
1,000 is ten hundreds.
check: How do you write "four hundred seven"?
What does the zero in 407 do?
lessons.try: Write 619 in words and in expanded form.

learn: Compare hundreds first, then tens, then ones.
523 > 489 because 5 hundreds is more than 4 hundreds.
361 < 367 because the hundreds and tens match, and 1 one is less than 7 ones.
lessons.try: Compare 708 and 780. Which is greater?

learn: Skip counting means counting by a number other than one.
Skip counting helps count money and tell time.
check: Six nickels is how many cents?
lessons.try: Count nickels by fives.

learn: Counting by hundreds: 100, 200, 300, up to 1,000.
You can start from other numbers: 150, 250, 350.
Only the hundreds digit changes.
check: When you count by hundreds, which digit changes?
lessons.try: Count by hundreds from 120 to 920.

learn: Skip counting makes equal jumps on a number line.
Starting at 0 with jumps of 5 lands on 5, 10, 15.
Finding the missing number: 35, 40, ?, 50. The jump is 5, so the answer is 45.
check: Skip counting makes jumps that are...
lessons.try: Draw a number line with jumps of 10 from 0 to 100.

learn: To add 34 + 25, add tens: 30 + 20 = 50. Add ones: 4 + 5 = 9. Total: 59.
Breaking numbers into tens and ones is called decomposing.
You can draw tens sticks and ones dots to show it.
check: Breaking numbers into tens and ones is called...
lessons.try: Add 42 + 36 by adding tens and ones.

learn: When the ones add to 10 or more, make a new ten. This is regrouping.
47 + 25: 7 + 5 = 12 ones, which is 1 ten and 2 ones. 40 + 20 + 10 = 70. Total: 72.
In written work, carry the new ten to the tens column.
check: When ones add to 10 or more, you...
lessons.try: Add 38 + 46 with regrouping.

learn: You can add up to four two-digit numbers.
Look for friendly numbers that make tens: 25 + 15 = 40.
Then add the rest: 40 + 33 = 73.
check: Which pair makes a friendly ten?

learn: To subtract 68 - 25, subtract tens: 60 - 20 = 40. Subtract ones: 8 - 5 = 3. Answer: 43.
Always subtract the smaller ones from the larger ones when you can.
Check by adding: 43 + 25 = 68.
lessons.try: Solve 79 - 34 and check with addition.

learn: Sometimes there are not enough ones. Break a ten into ten ones.
52 - 17: you can't take 7 from 2. Trade a ten: 4 tens and 12 ones. 12 - 7 = 5. 40 - 10 = 30. Answer: 35.
This is regrouping, sometimes called borrowing.
check: When there aren't enough ones, you...
lessons.try: Solve 63 - 28 with regrouping.

learn: Some problems need two steps.
"Mia had 45 stickers. She got 20 more, then gave 15 away. How many now?" 45 + 20 = 65. 65 - 15 = 50.
Read carefully, plan each step and check your answer makes sense.
check: Mia had 45, got 20, gave 15 away. How many now?
lessons.try: Make up a two-step story problem for a friend.

learn: Adding hundreds is like adding ones: 300 + 400 = 700.
253 + 400: only the hundreds change. 653.
10 more or 100 more: 10 more than 482 is 492. 100 more is 582.
lessons.try: Find 10 more, 10 less, 100 more and 100 less than 365.

learn: Add ones, then tens, then hundreds, regrouping when needed.
Line up the digits by place value.
check: How should you line up digits?

learn: Subtract ones, then tens, then hundreds, regrouping when needed.
542 - 187: 2 - 7 needs a ten: 12 - 7 = 5. 3 - 8 needs a hundred: 13 - 8 = 5. 4 - 1 = 3. Answer: 355.
Check by adding the answer to the number you subtracted.
lessons.try: Subtract 600 - 245.

learn: An inch is about the length of a paper clip. A foot is 12 inches, like a ruler.
Use inches for small things, like a pencil. Use feet for bigger things, like a door.
Line up the end of the object with the 0 mark on the ruler.
check: How many inches in a foot?
Which unit is best for a door?
lessons.try: Measure a pencil in inches and a table in feet.

learn: A centimetre is about the width of your fingertip. A metre is 100 centimetres.
Most countries use centimetres and metres.
The same object has more centimetres than inches because centimetres are smaller.
check: How many centimetres in a metre?
A centimetre is about the width of...
lessons.try: Measure your hand in centimetres.

learn: To estimate means to make a smart guess.
Then measure to check your estimate.
To compare, find the difference: a 9-inch book and a 6-inch book differ by 3 inches.
check: A 9-inch book and a 6-inch book differ by...
lessons.try: Estimate the length of a spoon, then measure it.

learn: The minute hand moves around the clock in 60 minutes.
Each number on the clock stands for 5 minutes: the 1 means 5, the 2 means 10, the 3 means 15.
When the hour hand is past 3 and the minute hand is on the 4, it is 3:20.
check: How many minutes in an hour?
When the minute hand points to 3, it is...
Hour hand past 3, minute hand on 4 is...
lessons.try: Read a clock at home at three different times.

learn: A.M. means the hours from midnight to noon. Morning.
P.M. means the hours from noon to midnight. Afternoon and evening.
You eat breakfast at 7:00 a.m. and dinner at 6:00 p.m.
lessons.try: Write three things you do and their times with a.m. or p.m.

learn: Penny 1¢, nickel 5¢, dime 10¢, quarter 25¢, dollar $1 = 100¢.
Count the biggest coins first: 2 quarters, 1 dime, 3 pennies = 25 + 25 + 10 + 3 = 63¢.
Use the cents sign ¢ or the dollar sign: $0.63.
check: How many cents in a dollar?
Which coins should you count first?
lessons.try: Count the coins in a pocket or jar.

learn: A bar graph uses bars to show data. A picture graph uses symbols.
Read the scale: in some picture graphs, one symbol might stand for 2.
You can answer questions like: how many more chose apples than bananas?
check: If one symbol stands for 2, how many do 4 symbols show?
Apples 9, bananas 5: how many more chose apples?
lessons.try: Survey 10 people about their favourite colour and make a bar graph.

learn: A polygon is a closed shape with straight sides.
Triangle 3 sides, quadrilateral 4, pentagon 5, hexagon 6.
A cube has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.
check: How many sides does a pentagon have?
A shape with 4 sides is a...
How many faces does a cube have?
lessons.try: Draw a pentagon and a hexagon.

learn: Shapes can be split into equal shares.
Two equal parts are halves. Three are thirds. Four are fourths.
Equal shares of the same shape don't have to look the same shape, just the same size.
check: Which is bigger: one half or one fourth of the same pizza?
Equal shares must be the same...
lessons.try: Fold paper into thirds and colour one third.
